correctness.rationale: Cyclic overlapping windows identify the words bijectively with labeled Euler tours modulo rotation in the corresponding residual de Bruijn digraph. Balance forces the omitted three edges to decompose into directed simple cycles (edge-disjoint); there are only two loops, one alternating two-cycle, and two primitive period-three cycles. A loop plus the alternating cycle affects distinct vertices for m≥2, as does each simple three-cycle, so no vertex is isolated by these deletions. For fixed residual graph, fixing one surviving first edge removes rotation with no stabilizer or extra factor. All active degrees are one or two, so BEST reduces to the directed tree count, including zero when disconnected. For balanced L, det(L+J) is N times a Laplacian cofactor on N vertices; the full chain satisfies P^m=J, giving cofactor 2^(N−1)/N and the displayed telescoping inverse. The two-cycle update is rank one; alternating suffix-prefix overlaps give 2(−1/2)^k on its signed endpoint vector. In the period-three case the determinant lemma gives K with row difference Z_i−Z_{i+1} along the deleted directed edges. All cyclic two-bit prefixes of the period are distinct, so only the last, one-bit overlap can match two phases. Independently recomputed the truncated geometric sums by subtracting their first excluded term; each K entry is affine in z in each residue class. Exact evaluations at four rational z values certify the full cubic-degree determinant identity in all three classes. At m=2 the period-three term is zero; for m≥3 it is strictly positive by the displayed formula, and the two-cycle term is positive for all m≥2. Direct rotation-canonical binary word enumeration gave totals 2 and 12 at n=3,4, split by combined types as (2,0) and (8,4). Summing the two complementary missing sets in each type and taking the limit gives the stated integer counts and proportions.
residual_risks: Direct word enumeration was only at n=3,4. The determinant identities were checked exactly as polynomial identities, and the graph proof supplies all n≥3.

evidence: Chen et al. study the probability that a deletion set admits a tour or trail, with exact results for up to two deletions or binary n≤4. Champlin et al. study existence for complementary classes. The indexed all-order two-defect counts are for q≥3 and shortfall two.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existence only tests whether the multiplicity is nonzero. Changing the alphabet or deleting two edges does not give the period-three update or its tree-count determinant. The classical BEST and matrix-tree framework applies but does not evaluate that determinant or the two type counts.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing which triples occur, or even their connectivity, does not give the rooted arborescence count for any triple. Evaluation of the alternating-cycle and phase-sensitive period-three updates yields new exact ratios, rather than a substitution into the earlier existence or finite counting statements.

evidence: Generalized de Bruijn words in the primary paper have maximal circular factor complexity and the paper counts modulo cyclic shift. The three-deletion universal-word record uses the same deleted edge language, while the nonpalindromic-factor record covers only a prescribed set of three-letter factors.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: At length 2^n−3 the distinct length-n windows give maximal complexity. For shorter windows all 2^(n−1) words occur because each length-(n−1) vertex remains active, and longer windows are distinct because the length-n windows are distinct. Thus the generalized-de-Bruijn table uses the same equivalence and indeed has matching entries. Linear words and factor sets defined by a nonpalindromic predicate are different objects.

value.rationale: Three missing windows are a natural next exact deficit for near-universal binary cycles. The formula answers how many cycles survive, not merely whether they survive, and reveals a nontrivial split between the two admissible missing patterns, a sharp zero at minimal order, and a limiting comparison with full cycles. A future enumeration can use these exact per-type counts in place of exponentially large Euler-tour or cofactor computations.
residual_risks: Scope is labeled binary factors, shortfall exactly three, and oriented cycles modulo rotations only; no formula is implied for arbitrary deficits.
